function: Diffusion-based DDPG learns V2V channel allocation, vehicle power control and UAV altitude adjustment to maximize the V2U sum rate under delayed CSI (p. 1)
system: Single UAV aerial base station, vehicles on a 2 km highway, scalar fading channels (antennas not stated), OFDM at 5.9 GHz, 2 MHz channels; no RIS (pp. 3-4, 10)
method: Diffusion-based deep deterministic policy gradient (D3PG): MLP denoiser as actor plus MLP critic; reinforcement learning with a Lyapunov drift-plus-penalty reward, 500 training episodes (pp. 7-10)
data_channel: Simulated: SUMO vehicle traces on an OpenStreetMap highway in Xiamen; LoS/NLoS path loss with elevation-angle LoS probability, Rayleigh small-scale fading, Gauss-Markov delayed CSI (pp. 4, 9)
test_conditions: Trained 500 episodes on SUMO traffic; five random seeds; sweeps of V2V links (6-10), CSI delay (2-10 ms), Lyapunov weight; no unseen-condition test stated (pp. 10-12)
baselines: DDPG (MLP actor), D3PG-WCSI (no CSI-delay model), H-DDQN [8] (Hungarian channel allocation plus DDQN for power and altitude) (pp. 9-10)
metrics: V2U communication sum rate, episodic reward, UAV propulsion energy, virtual energy queue length, running time per slot (pp. 10-12)
complexity: O(ST*I*L*n^2) total and O(I*L*n^2) per slot for the denoiser; running time 2.64-3.34 ms per slot for 6-10 V2V links (pp. 9, 12)
q1_support: p. 4: "combining large-scale path loss and Rayleigh small-scale fading" (own channel model); p. 9: "The SUMO simulator [17] is then used to generate moving" vehicles. No 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel data.
q2_support: p. 10: "(i.e., using five different random seeds)" is the only variation of the environment in the averaging; no statement that a trained model is tested in a scenario, configuration or dataset unseen in training.
q3_support: p. 9: "we have relied on three benchmark solutions" (DDPG, D3PG-WCSI, H-DDQN); p. 10: "Hungarian and DDQN-based resource allocation algorithm" mixes the Hungarian algorithm with DDQN. All are learning-based or variants of D3PG; no purely non-learned baseline.
q4_support: p. 9: "the total computational complexity of the proposed D3PG algorithm is O(ST ILn2 )"; Table III on p. 12 also reports the running time per time slot in milliseconds.
q5_support: p. 9: "The SUMO simulator [17] is then used to generate moving" vehicles on an OpenStreetMap road; simulated data, no code or data link, no public channel dataset or measured data.
notes: Area 6: learned power control and channel allocation for a UAV aerial base station are physical-layer decisions, learned jointly with altitude adjustment, so the above-PHY exclusion does not apply (p. 1). The extracted text of pp. 10-13 was incomplete, so those pages were read as images (Table II, Figs. 6-11, Table III). q1: the abstract speaks of real-world vehicle mobility traces, but the body says SUMO generates the vehicles on an OpenStreetMap road (p. 9), and the channel is a custom model; the reviewer may confirm. q3: H-DDQN [8] combines the Hungarian algorithm with DDQN and D3PG-WCSI is a variant of the proposed method, so no purely non-learned baseline was counted; the reviewer may confirm. Version read is the arXiv v1 preprint (2507.20524v1).
